correctness.rationale: Exact triangular matrix and norm normalization reconstructed; moments yield \(m_n\sim\Gamma(s)n^{-s}(\log n)^{-\gamma}\) and b_j-square sum \(n^{2s-1}/((2s-1)\Gamma(s)^2)\). Their product gives positive row constant \(1/(2s-1)\) with locally uniform \(O(1/\log n)\) error for gamma near one half. Classical weighted Cesàro bound, compact diagonal and weakly-null block arguments prove the sharp boundedness/compactness boundary; integral comparisons yield S2 and exact coefficients. originality.rationale: The full 2026 Blasco–Pennanen Bergman-kernel Cesàro source proves boundedness on function spaces, not the output-row Schatten 2 spectrum or this exact logarithmic coefficient. The critical beta-function operator norm is classical and not asserted original. The principal novelty is the simultaneous compactness threshold \(\gamma>0\), Hilbert–Schmidt threshold \(\gamma>1/2\), all sharp truncated-row constants and the parameter-boundary blow-up. Closest searched claims use a different target space (Bergman balls in dimension >=2) or different Cesàro kernels. value.rationale: The logarithmic perturbation of the critical Hardy/Bergman-kernel Cesàro measure is a canonical and mathematically motivated boundary test. It distinguishes the compactness condition \(\gamma>0\) from a genuinely stricter S2 condition \(\gamma>1/2\) over a full open interval, and supplies an exact universal sharp trace-divergence coefficient and parameter-edge blow-up for arbitrary real Bergman kernel exponent \(s>1\). The already-known critical order-s Cesàro norm is explicitly credited; the value rests on the new quantitative operator-ideal separation.
